pr_comments: Oh hey, I remember being annoyed by this and not being able to figure out how to fix it when I was working on the MVP one-shot systems. Definitely a bug.

issue_context.title: One shot system cannot recursively call itself
comments:
> I think this happens cause the system may be removed from the world while it's executed

Yup. The problem is that applying a command queue requires exclusive access to it (both because running commands consumes them and to clear the queue), and a system's command queue is stored in the system itself.

To fix this, I think need to move the command queue out of the system and then double buffer them. Iirc flecs uses a thread-local queue?

> Apparently i can just go with observers since i was told they can recursivly call themself, which i tried to avoid since in my use case it's mean 500 entities, one for each effect), but in the end it's probably nothing and have 0 perf issue.

Should be fine, as entities shouldn't hurt performance just by existing.

> There's a note about this on [`World::run_system`](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/struct.World.html#method.run_system).
> 
> After some testing it looks like you _can_ make it work with a custom `System` implementation that unconditionally uses `System::queue_deferred` instead of `System::apply_deferred`. This may have other consequences, so I wouldn't recommend it.

Guess i have to use Observer for anything that can call itself, haven't tested them yet so i hope they support recursive.

Entities have 0 cost if they do nothing right ? (outside the few bits of memory), i can have as many observers i want ?


Also i'm not sure if i should close this issue. Not rly used to the github ecosystem to know.
Definitely a bug! Please leave this open.

review_comments: I thought commands were only run at sync points? Not after any system has been run?

We are at a sync point, in the sense that we have an exclusive reference to the world. Before this PR, commands queued by the system were executed here via `System::run`.

There is a difference in behavior though: Previously, only the commands queued by the system were applied (which might include running other systems and their commands); now, this includes commands that were already queued before the system was run. I've documented it, but if we think the previous behavior is less surprising, I'll add a method to `CommandQueue` to only apply part of it and use it here. I'd do that in a followup PR though because it also involves unsafe and I want to keep it easy to review.
All good I mostly asked for my own understanding.

This is a useful API to expose!  The single-threaded executor has some unsafe code and a special case for exclusive systems because it wants exactly this behavior: 

https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/b73811d40e477503119d13f423fc49bcaec2af42/crates/bevy_ecs/src/schedule/executor/single_threaded.rs#L116

It might be worth doing a follow-up to use `run_without_applying_deferred` there.
